_readme.covers: Units 16-21. Chain progressions by 5ths and 3rds, diatonic sequences, minor v in major, consonant 6/4 classification, and a heuristic for unresolved accented non-chord tones.
_readme.structure: Every rule has: rule_id, tier, category, weight, error_message, check.
_readme.note_on_figuration: Units 20-21 (passing tones, neighbors, suspensions, anticipations, pedal points) are not fully modelled because the harmony slice-builder currently treats every sounding note as a chord tone. P4-ACCENTED-NCT is a best-effort heuristic.
_readme.note_on_sequences: Ascending 5th motions are suppressed inside recognised sequences (Unit 17). The P4-ASC-THIRD-WEAK rule was deleted because ascending 3rd root motion is extremely common and musically legitimate in I-iii, IV-vi, and ii-IV progressions; it is a quality characteristic, not a fault.
how_to_add_a_rule: 1. Copy a rule block between { and }.
2. Give it a new unique rule_id.
3. Choose a check.type that a pass module has registered.
6. Save. No trailing comma after the last rule.

rules.error_message: Root motion by ascending 5th is a retrogression — the tonal current flows by descending 5th and descending 3rd
Minor v in a major key — a modal colouring that departs from the diatonic dominant
6/4 chord with no idiomatic function — should be cadential, passing, neighboring, or arpeggiated
Accented non-chord tone that does not resolve as a suspension — check that this note is properly prepared and resolved
